subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw own a stable cross-language agent-runtime compatibility contract for standalone non-Node hosts, including bare-metal devices?
rationale: Current main exposes reusable TypeScript internals and host-coupled extension seams, but repository vision does not determine whether independent runtimes should be OpenClaw-compatible products.

options.title: Sponsor runtime protocol
options.body: Define and version the minimal host/runtime contract with conformance tests, using MimiClaw as prior art and a constrained reference implementation.

options.title: Keep Node-hosted scope
options.body: State that OpenClaw remains a TypeScript and Node orchestration host, treating embedded projects as independent ports without compatibility guarantees.

options.title: Defer behind JSON-RPC
options.body: Wait for the language-agnostic plugin ABI and then reassess only the remaining standalone-host gap.

recommendation.title: Sponsor runtime protocol
recommendation.body: Define and version the minimal host/runtime contract with conformance tests, using MimiClaw as prior art and a constrained reference implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and merged runtime-architecture history make this the strongest available product/API decision owner.
